title: Decide per-target denials before the delegate escape can fail open
judge_obligation_ack: standard lane: feature-close independent review pass covers the judge read

truths: With .bee/companion-session.json present, a command mixing a shell-syntax target and a containment-failing literal target DENIES (exit 2) instead of delegating fail-open, in both target orders (the ADV-A/ADV-B probes become tests)
The same holds when guards.memory_root is declared instead of the marker

A command whose ONLY undecidable target genuinely needs delegation still delegates — the change never converts a legitimate lone delegate into a deny of an allowed write, and never allows anything previously denied

action: Per CONTEXT.md D2: restructure the Bash per-target loop in main.rs so native verdicts (shell-syntax denial, containment denial) are decided and retained BEFORE any Err(Nd) from companion_mount_rel or memory_root_hit can escape as Outcome::Delegate — if any target already produced a native denial, the hook returns that denial; Nd escapes only when no denial exists. Mirror the same ordering on the Edit branch (main.rs:290/:300) where the identical class lives. Red-first tests from probes ADV-A/ADV-B (both orders, marker and memory_root variants) plus a control proving a lone legitimately-delegating payload still delegates.
acceptance: All three must_haves truths hold with named tests; suite green
